questions.passage: Jenny remembered when her two-year-old daughter had come across a small wallaby and how she had said, 'There's a baby kangaroo, Mummy!' She had seen plenty of kangaroos when they went to the farm to see Kate. She explained to her daughter that a wallaby was like a kangaroo, but smaller. Wallaby became Sara's new word and her understanding of the world grew a little more.
questions.markingGuide: Accept 'Sara'. The passage says 'Wallaby became Sara's new word' — Sara is the daughter. The tricky part is that 'Jenny' is the mother and 'Kate' is likely someone at the farm (aunt/friend). Reject 'Jenny' (that's the mother) or 'Kate' (that's someone they visit at the farm, not the daughter).
